top_story.headline: Raskin Bill Would Put Trump-Era "Authoritarianism" in a Permanent Smithsonian Exhibit
top_story.dek: On a two-minute House session with no votes, Rep. Jamie Raskin filed the most politically charged of the day's 22 measures.
paragraphs: H.R. 10765 directs the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution to collect, preserve and display, in a permanent exhibition at the National Museum of American History, artifacts reflecting "the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism" during Donald J. Trump's two presidencies. Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) is the sponsor; the bill lists no cosponsors in the Congressional Record.

The bill text defines the second term as running through January 20, 2029. It was referred to the Committee on House Administration, and in addition to the Committee on Natural Resources. No action beyond referral has been recorded.
The House met at 4 p.m. on October 6, 2026, and adjourned at 4:02 p.m. with no votes, so introductions were the day's only substantive record.

sections.headline: House Meets Two Minutes, Introduces 22 Measures; Senate in Pro Forma Session
paragraphs: The House met at 4 p.m. on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, and adjourned at 4:02 p.m.; there were no recorded votes, roll call votes or quorum calls. Committee reports were filed on H.R. 6698 (Board of Veterans' Appeals annual report) and H.R. 7260 (National Cemetery Administration annual report). The Senate held a 33-second pro forma session and adjourned until 1:30 p.m. on Friday, October 9, 2026.

Seventeen bills, one concurrent resolution and four simple resolutions were introduced, all in the House. Beyond H.R. 10765, the most newsworthy include H.R. 10759, a tariff-funded relief program for U.S. manufacturers and farmers; H.Res. 1618, marking the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks on Israel; and H.R. 10767, an excise tax on schools over athlete eligibility. Every measure is listed below.

items: H.R. 10751, sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI-1) with Rep. Tom Cole and Rep. Sharice Davids — lifts restrictions on dental therapist services under the Indian Health Care Improvement Act's Community Health Aide Program. Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10752, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — creates an artificial intelligence task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Referred to the Committee on Homeland Security.

H.R. 10753, the Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — lets housing agencies voluntarily reallocate vouchers under the Tribal HUD-VASH program. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10754, the Rural Disaster Fairness Act of 2026, sponsored by Crane (R-AZ-2) — updates indicators of a disaster's local impact under the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018. Referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10755, sponsored by Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30) — names the post office at 475 East FM 1382 in Cedar Hill, Texas, the "Eugene Gates Jr. Post Office Building." Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
H.R. 10756, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) with Rep. Suzanne Bonamici — reauthorizes Regional Ocean Partnerships. Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10757, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) with Rep. Michael Lawler — limits U.S. contributions to the United Nations. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10758, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-3) with Rep. Maggie Goodlander — directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to award grants to state entities for structured outdoor recreation programs for veterans. Referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10759, sponsored by Rep. John James (R-MI-10) — sets up a tariff-funded program to shield U.S. manufacturers, workers and farmers from economic harm caused by tariffs and foreign retaliation. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10760, sponsored by Rep. Thomas H. Kean (R-NJ-7) — creates a Middle School Mental Health Task Force across the Department of Education and the Department of Health and Human Services. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10761, the Campus Accountability and Safety Act of 2026, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) with Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick and others — amends the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act to combat campus sexual assault. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10762, the Anthony Amoros Law Right to Know Act, sponsored by Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY-17) — requires used-car sellers to keep a vehicle's airbag system functional or clearly disclose when it is missing or disabled. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10763, the Know Your Risk Act, sponsored by Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA-5) — orders a Department of Health and Human Services report on breast cancer risk assessment tools. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10764, the Executive Settlement Review Act, sponsored by Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI-4) — requires certain procedures for compromise settlements or awards paid to executive branch officials. Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10765, sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) — directs the Smithsonian Institution to display a permanent National Museum of American History exhibition on the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption and authoritarianism during Donald J. Trump's two presidencies. Referred to the Committee on House Administration and the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10766, sponsored by Rep. Keith Self (R-TX-3) — directs the Secretary of Defense to add assets critical to the Golden Dome missile defense system to the Department of Defense Critical Asset List. Referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10767, the Fair Play Enforcement Act, sponsored by Rep. Adrian Smith (R-NE-3) with Rep. Brendan Boyle — imposes an excise tax on colleges and universities that let specified individuals take part in intercollegiate athletics. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H. Con. Res. 123, sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) with 22 cosponsors — recognizes the wage disparity facing Latinas and its effect on women, families and the economy. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
H.Res. 1617, sponsored by Rep. Earl L. "Buddy" Carter (R-GA-1) with Rep. Diana Harshbarger — recognizes October as "American Pharmacy Month." Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.Res. 1618, sponsored by Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) with dozens of bipartisan cosponsors — marks the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel, honors victims and hostages, and calls for the complete disarmament of Hamas. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1619, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA-15) with Rep. William Keating — reaffirms German-American friendship and supports continued cooperation with Germany. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1620, sponsored by Rep. Nikema Williams (D-GA-5) — supports the goals of "National Nonviolence Week" to raise awareness of youth violence. Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
